creative.body:
My sister Diane quit Wegovy at month 4. Down 28 pounds and gaining momentum. She did not quit because the medication failed. She quit because the constipation was so bad she said it felt like she had swallowed a brick that would not pass, and her doctor's only answer was "eat more fiber."

That was 14 months ago.

She has gained back every pound and 11 more. She has spent the year since trying every diet, every cleanse, every program she can find, and not 1 of them has touched what the GLP-1 was doing for her.

Last month I almost made her exact decision.

This is the story of the 2 of us, running on parallel tracks 5 months apart, and the phone call that kept me from finishing the track Diane finished.

Here is what happened to my sister.

Month 4. Diane is down 28 pounds. The fastest she has ever lost weight in her life. She is also up to 4 Miralax doses a day, prune juice with breakfast, magnesium citrate every night, and the brick in her abdomen that will not pass. She tells her doctor she cannot live like this. The doctor tells her to eat more fiber. Diane goes home that afternoon and throws her pen in the trash.

Month 6. 8 pounds back. Her A1C creeping. She tells Frank she is going to white-knuckle it with diet and exercise this time. She joins a gym. She joins Noom. She joins a meal service that ships portion-controlled boxes to the porch.

Month 10. 18 pounds back. She has tried 3 cleanses, 2 elimination diets, a 30-day juice protocol, and a hypnotherapist a friend swore by. None of it has touched the appetite the way the pen did. She is hungry every hour she is awake.

Month 14. 28 pounds back, and 11 more on top. Sleep apnea returned. Knees hurting again. Her primary care wants her back on a GLP-1. Her insurance has dropped her in the meantime. To start over, out of pocket, is $1,300 a month. Diane has been sitting at her kitchen table at night, head in her hands, doing the math.

That is Diane's track.

Now mine.

I'm 54. I started Wegovy 5 months after Diane quit. I had watched her go down and then back up and I told myself I was going to do it differently. I was going to be smart. I was going to read the patient communities. I was going to stay on top of the side effects from week 1.

Down 31 pounds. The most weight I have ever lost in my life. My knees stopped hurting. My A1C dropped almost a full point. My husband pulled out a pair of jeans I had not worn in 9 years and they fit.

And last month I had the pen in my hand on a Sunday night, already loaded.

Instead of injecting it I set it down on the bathroom counter.

I sat down on the closed lid of the toilet and stared at the pen on the counter for 20 minutes.

I had not had a normal bowel movement in 12 days. The constipation had given me bleeding hemorrhoids the week before. My abdomen felt like a brick by 4pm every afternoon. I had considered driving myself to the ER twice in 9 days. I was sleeping in a recliner because lying flat made the pressure under my ribs unbearable.

The math had flipped.

I had been telling myself for 4 months that the misery was the price of the weight loss, and it had been worth it.

Until that Sunday night, when it suddenly wasn't.

The pen sat on the counter all of Monday. I did not throw it in the trash, but I did not pick it up either. Diane had thrown hers in the trash on a Monday too.

Tuesday morning my phone rang at 7:14am.

It was Frank.

Diane's husband. My brother-in-law of 22 years.

Frank does not call me. Frank texts me on birthdays and lets Diane handle the rest. In 22 years he has called my phone maybe 6 times.

I picked up because I thought somebody had died.

He apologized for calling. He said Diane had told him on Sunday night that I had been talking about quitting my pen.

He said he had been quietly reading on Reddit and PubMed and the GLP-1 forums every weekend for 14 months trying to figure out what had happened to his wife.

He said he was not a doctor. He was a guy who reads.

He said he had finally pieced it together a few weeks ago. He had not known how to bring it up to Diane without making her feel like he had taken too long.

And then he said the thing that made me sit down at my kitchen table.

"If you make the same decision Diane made, I am going to spend the rest of my life knowing I should have called sooner. So I'm calling now. Please don't put your pen down before you hear me out."

I told him I was listening.

This is what Frank said.

"The medication works in 2 places. The brain part, the appetite suppression, that is the engine of your weight loss, you do not want to undo it. The stomach part is the side effect, and your stomach is what slowed down to nearly frozen, which is why the food sits there for 10 or 12 hours and ferments and causes every symptom you have. Every product Diane's doctor and your doctor have ever told you to take, Miralax, magnesium, fiber, suppositories, all of them work on the colon, 6 feet downstream from where the actual problem is sitting. The protocol you have been on is working on the wrong organ. There is a compound called apigenin that works on the stomach wall instead. That is the whole answer."

5 sentences.

14 months of weekend reading, on a phone call, in 5 sentences.

I sat with the phone against my ear and I could hear him breathing on the other end and I started crying.

He told me the formulation he had landed on was a small company called Motilli. Standardized apigenin extract from celery juice, not powder. Combined with chlorophyllin to bind the sulfur compounds the bacteria were producing in my stalled stomach, and a small targeted dose of soluble prebiotic fiber for the lower gut once the upstream was moving again.

He said Diane had started Motilli 3 weeks earlier. He said for the first time in 14 months she had gone on her own on a Tuesday morning and called him into the bathroom to tell him.

He said, "I should have figured this out a year ago. Pick up your pen tonight."

I picked the pen up off the bathroom counter that Tuesday night and took my Sunday dose 5 days late. First time in 5 months I did it without dread.

The first 4 days on Motilli, nothing. I texted Frank and told him it wasn't working. He wrote back, "Same as Diane on day 4."

Around the second week the pressure under my ribs by 4pm stopped being sharp.

Around the third week I went on my own for the first time in 5 months without forcing it. I sat on the edge of the tub afterward and could not remember the last time my body had done that.

By week 6 the Miralax, the magnesium, the fiber gummies, the psyllium husk, all of it was off my counter and in a trash bag. My husband walked into the bathroom and saw the empty counter and said, "Took you long enough."

I am at month 8 of Wegovy now. Down 38 pounds and going. The math never flipped back, because the suffering side of the equation finally stopped growing.

Diane is back on Wegovy too. On Motilli with it. She is paying $1,300 a month out of pocket because her insurance dropped her during the year she spent off the medication, and she is not sure when she'll be able to get it covered again. She told me last week that she would pay $1,300 a month for the rest of her life before she would let her sleep apnea and her knees and the brick come back. She said the pen and the gummies together cost her less than the year of cleanses and meal services and hypnotherapy did, and a fraction of what gaining the weight back cost her body.

That is the trade nobody told either of us about.

Quitting the pen is not free. Diane paid for it in 39 pounds, an A1C jump, sleep apnea, knees, $1,300 a month, and 14 months of her life she will not get back.

If you are 1 week from making her decision, please read this twice and then make Frank's call to yourself before you make hers.

The mechanism is simple once someone explains it.

The medication works in 2 places. Brain part is the engine. Don't undo it. Stomach part is where every symptom is coming from. Every product on every shelf works 6 feet downstream. Apigenin works on the right organ.

Motilli is the formulation Frank read his way to over 14 months trying to save his wife. 90-day money-back guarantee. Small batch because apigenin degrades from light and heat, and the bottles sell out for stretches when more women in the GLP-1 communities find them. If you have a vacation, a holiday, a wedding coming up, I would not wait until next week.

The link is below.

— Carolyn Month 8 of Wegovy, and someone who picked her pen back up because Frank picked up his phone

P.S. Frank's voice on the phone that morning was not the voice of the brother-in-law who texts me on birthdays. It was the voice of a man who had been crying for an hour before he dialed and was trying not to let me hear it. I heard it anyway. I will hear it for the rest of my life.
